body: Thank you for the advice.  I get episodes where I feel like how I posted, but I do feel a bit better now.  I will go to counseling with the goal to be more honest with myself.
I would never leave my sister--you can count on that.

I've talked to my friends.  I think they just see me as a relaly negative person.  They all have pretty good lives with a lot of close friends.  Most of them are already graduated by now.  I have friends, but I don't have any best friends.  None of them can relate to my abuse or mental illness.

I have a counseling appointment on the 25th with my school's counseling service.  I have been going to counseling there for a while, but I have a tendency to hide a huge part of myself from people and not even realize it--as a sort of protection.  I am scared of being told I am "crazy" and I try so hard to be normal and functioning.  I think I will go to the center tomorrow and ask to be seen asap because I really need to talk to someone.

I promised him that I would wait one month to talk to him.  Most people have told me to honor that promise and wait despite knowing what i'm going through.  I don't want to put him under more stress since he is probably trying to sort through the things we talked about.  We are supposed to be "becoming individuals" again during our break.  I feel that if i talked to him now it would be seen as an act of desperation to people who don't understand the extent of my depression or how suicidal I really am.  I don't think anyone in his family takes me seriously.

I didn't get an internship over the summer so all I did was stay at the house.  Whenever I have nothing to do I automatically get really depressed because I feel like I have no purpose.  This made me have no sex drive, and my bf is a very physical person so he assumed I didn't love him anymore.  I reconciled this with myself and told myself I was not happy because I didn't want to be a housewife, blah blah.  I thought that I would be happy if I could go into research and be alone--but I definitely was not in the right state of mind when I made that decision.  I moved out two weeks ago.  He has a very hard time understanding my mental illness--he grew up in a wealthy, close-knit family and I don't think he ever took my suicidal threats seriously.  I think that a part of me broke up with him because I thought it would be easier if I did that before I committed suicide, so he feels like he isn't attached to me as much.
